Tuition & Financial Aid
Tuition & Financial Aid
Now’s the time to invest in yourself. Learn more about graduate tuition costs and the wide range of funding opportunities available to help make your goals a reality.
Getting started
U.S. citizens should first consider starting their Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA), the first step toward receiving financial support from the federal government.
Next, all students should visit our Student Financial Services (SFS) website for more details on current tuition costs, aid opportunities, and how to apply. Tuition and fees vary based on the program and may change yearly.
For additional questions, connect with an enrollment counselor who can help you evaluate the costs associated with your program of choice.
For information regarding tuition and fees for students studying at Canadian campuses, visit the Student Accounts Canada website.
See tuition and fees
Learn how to apply for graduate aid
Speak to an enrollment counselor
Financial aid
Fund your future
A graduate education at Northeastern is an investment in your future; it shouldn’t have to be a financial burden in the present.
We offer a wide range of opportunities to help fund your studies, including scholarships, grants, and fellowships. With more than $437 million in financial aid awarded to our students during the 2023—2024 academic year, we’re committed to helping you find the financial aid solutions that can keep you on course toward your professional goals.
Scholarships
Our graduate scholarships are designed to help you pursue your goals without taking on debt. Discover untapped sources of financial aid through university-sponsored scholarships, college merit scholarships, and more.
Explore scholarships
Military benefits
We offer substantial tuition assistance to active servicemembers and veterans, including unlimited institutional matching funds to eligible graduate students through the Yellow Ribbon Program.
See military benefits
Fellowships
Fellowships offer graduate students the opportunity to apply their talents at research centers, universities, and nonprofit organizations worldwide.
Discover fellowship opportunities
Assistantships
Assistantships are another great way to engage with your field of research as you learn. Certain assistantship opportunities will be arranged upon acceptance of your application; other program opportunities might be awarded at any time.
These opportunities include:
Research assistantships (RA) are funded through externally arranged grants—RAs research with the support of regular faculty members.
Teaching assistantships (TA) are ideal for students who wish to engage with the broader student body, including undergraduates. TAs help faculty members with coursework and instruction.
Stipend graduate assistantships include a stipend, tuition remission, and health plans for eligible doctoral students.
Learn more about assistantships
